title: Babylon
summary: Babylon, on the Euphrates 85 km south of Baghdad, was a minor port city until Hammurabi (reigned 1792-1750 BCE) made it his capital. It was capital of the Neo-Babylonian Empire from 626 to 539 BCE under rulers such as Nebuchadnezzar, then of the Achaemenid Empire after Cyrus took it, until Alexander the Great in 331 BCE. UNESCO inscribed its ruins, walls, gates, palaces and temples in 2019.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia: the city is older than Sargon of Akkad (reign 2334-2279 BCE) and became a capital under Hammurabi (1792 BCE); it fell to Alexander in 331 BCE and continued as a trade centre afterwards. UNESCO dates the Neo-Babylonian capital phase to 626-539 BCE.

phases.description: Ishtar Gate built by Nebuchadnezzar II, circa 575 BCE.
Gate stands as the main entrance to Babylon; the end date is the rediscovery of the ruins by Robert Koldewey in 1899, not a dated collapse.
Ruins rediscovered and excavated by Robert Koldewey from 1899; the gate itself was later rebuilt in the Pergamon Museum, Berlin, and a reconstruction was attempted at Babylon.
